landing_meta_description: Tonnr is a free, open-source surf app. Read buoys, forecasts and tides on one map, save your spots, and be told when the conditions that make them work line up.
landing_hero_body: Buoys, forecasts and tides on one map. Save a spot with the conditions that make it work, and be told when they line up.
landing_hero_note: Free. No account needed to read the map.
landing_shot_alt: The Tonnr map off western Europe: the sea colored by its wave height, the buoys with their latest reading, and the panel of the Belle-Ile buoy, whose curves stand beside the model's.
landing_shot_credits: Tonnr on 13 October 2026. Map: OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles, OpenStreetMap. Sea: E.U. Copernicus Marine Service. Buoys: the public networks the app names.
landing_alert_more: Say what makes a spot work, and {name} tells you when the sea agrees.
landing_alert_note: Checked against the measurements and seven days of forecast. Told by mail or by push: the evening before, and when it begins.
landing_features_more: The map is open to everyone. An account is for what you keep. Sign in with email, or with Google when the instance offers it.

sources_irish_lights_text: The buoys and weather stations of the Irish lighthouse service. Waves and wind.
sources_marine_institute_text: The weather buoys far off the Irish coast, M2 to M6. Waves and wind.
sources_hidrografico_text: The wave buoys of the Portuguese Navy's hydrographic institute.
sources_fmi_text: The wave buoys of the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
sources_queensland_text: The wave buoys of the Queensland Government, along its coast.
sources_meteo_france_text: The ground stations of the French weather service: wind and gusts.
sources_openwindmap_text: A community network of wind beacons, Pioupiou among them, often set right on the spots.
sources_dmi_text: The stations of the Danish weather service, many on lighthouses and harbours: wind and gusts.
sources_rijkswaterstaat_text: The stations of the Dutch authority of the coast: on the shore, on the Wadden and on the platforms of the North Sea.
sources_jma_text: AMeDAS, the automatic stations of the Japanese weather service, many on capes and harbours.
sources_coops_text: The weather sensors of NOAA's tide stations, on piers and harbours, on the shore itself: wind and gusts.
sources_ipma_text: The stations of the Portuguese weather institute, every hour.
sources_aemet_text: The automatic stations of the Spanish weather agency, with gusts, on an instance that holds a key.
sources_metar_text: The reports of the world's airports, where no other station stands near: wind and gusts.
sources_open_meteo_text: Wave and wind forecasts at any point, from the models of ECMWF, at 9 km, and of Météo-France, at 8 km, with the weather to come.
sources_copernicus_models_text: The Met Office's fine model, at 1.5 km from the Vendée to Norway; the swell apart from the wind sea, by Météo-France's model; and the map of wave heights.

sources_catalogue_text: The breaks the instance's operator added, completed by what accounts write of them. A spot an account makes public joins it under the ODbL.
sources_openfreemap_text: The map under everything, drawn from OpenStreetMap.
sources_natural_earth_text: The coastline that tells a wind station of the coast from one inland, so that a wide view shows the sea's wind first.
sources_photon_text: Finding a place by its name, for an account.
sources_missing_text: Tell me which one, and where it publishes. The technical detail of every source, its access and its terms, is in the repository.
landing_agents_more: The map's data is an API and an MCP server. Plug your agent in, and ask it about the sea.
landing_agents_mcp_text: Read-only tools over Streamable HTTP, with one key and the limits of the API.
landing_agents_page_more: What a program reads of the sea, and how it starts.
landing_agents_body: Buoys and their readings, forecasts at any point, tides, and the catalogue of breaks with their guides, each answer with its source and its licence. An agent plugs in by MCP, or reads one file that says what Tonnr is and how to call it. Signed in as you, an assistant also reads your spots, your alerts and your sessions, and changes nothing.
landing_agents_llms_text: What Tonnr is and how to call it, in plain text.
landing_agents_spec_text: Every route and its types, for a program.
landing_agents_docs_text: The same routes, for a person.
landing_agents_key_text: I hand the keys out myself. Tell me what you are building.
landing_agents_prompt: Read {url}, then use the Tonnr API to tell me what the sea does at my spot over the next three days: swell, wind and tide.
landing_story_me: I'm Téo. I love two things: building software and surfing.
landing_story_origin_after: , the app Thomas Cailhol built in Biarritz. I loved what it does and how it is made. It showed me that a developer who surfs can build the tool he wants to use. So I started mine, to add my own touch: my spots, the conditions that make each of them work, and a word when they line up. Thank you, Thomas, for the inspiration and for showing it could be done.
landing_story_feedback: Tonnr is one person's project. It is free, open source, and only getting started, so it will be wrong in places: a buoy that reads strangely, a forecast that misses, a screen that makes no sense. I need you to tell me. Every message makes the next version better.
landing_next_more: Nothing here is promised. Tell me which one you want first.
landing_next_mobile_text: iOS and Android, with alerts that reach your pocket.
landing_next_data_text: Networks still to check, and a fuller catalogue of spots.
landing_next_tides_text: Closer to the official predictions, where they can be used.

analytics_description: The app is just getting started. These analytics help me understand what works and where people get stuck. Your spot locations, searches and written content are never sent.
analytics_terms: With your permission, usage analytics sends PostHog an opaque account or device ID, technical session identifiers and the features you use. Your spot locations, searches and written content are excluded. Refusing does not limit the app. Change your choice in the account settings.
